the addition of aerobic digester effluent to the anaerobic fermenter significantly improved stability of the anaerbic digester, increased the volatile solids reduction, and increased the dewaterability.
the addition of a postaerotic digester to a two stage digester system improves the VSR, improves the biogas production, and improves the biogases quality.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of a two stage anaerbic digester system by using an aerobic digester as a means of recycling nutrients back into the anaerobic process.

the effects of aerobic digestion on the stability of the two stage anaerobically digested sludge, the effects of aerobic recycle stream on the two stage anaero bically digested sludges, and the effects of aerobic digester temperature on the stability of two stage anaer obically digested sludes.
the optimization of the recycle flow rate to maximize the stability and efficiency of the two stage anaerobicsystem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a postaerobeic digester can significantly improve the stability of an anaerobic digested, and that this can be accomplished with a recycle stream.
a two stage anaerbic digestion system can be successfully coupled with aerobic digestion to improve the overall performance of the anaerobicsystem.
the aerobic digestion recycle stream to the anaerobic digestion process was found to be beneficial in the overall process, however, the recycle rate needs to be optimized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the addition of a postaerobidigester following an anaerobic digested improved the stability and performance of the anaerobidigested, however the recycle rate from aerobic digester to fermenting digester did not have a large effect on the performance of the anaerbiodigester.
we were able to improve the stability and performance of our two stage anaerobically digested wastewater.
the addition of aerobic digestion to anaerbic digestion with a recycle rate of 50% of the anaerobically digested sludge was able to increase the VSR of the system from 30% to 45%.
The main takeaway from our work is that

aerobic digestion can be used to significantly reduce the oxygen demand in the postaerobic anaerobic digested sludge, therefore reducing the overall energy required to operate the postaerobically digested sludge.
aerobic digestion of the effluent from the anaerobic digestion can significantly improve the stability of anaerobic digestions, therefore improving overall performance of the system.
a recycle rate of 10% from an aerobic digester to a fermenting anaerobic digested significantly improved the stability and performance of the anaerobically digested sludge.
